issues.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] qwen3: Reuse fused QK-norm/RoPE kernel for decode
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3's native CUDA decode path launches QK normalization and RoPE separately. Reuse the existing table-based QK-norm/RoPE kernel to perform both operations in place, eliminating one launch per layer and the intervening Q/K write/read without introducing a new kernel.

On Qwen3-8B, this removes 36 launches per decode step. Eight paired B200 runs before merging main measured ~1.76% lower decode latency at concurrency 1 and ~0.81% at concurrency 32. 


## Modifications

- Add an opt-in `match_cuda` mode to `table_qk_norm_rope_`. It reproduces the separate CUDA kernels' reduction order, reciprocal square root, intermediate BF16 rounding, and RoPE multiply/FMA ordering. The existing default mode remains unchanged for existing callers.
- Route eligible Qwen3 native CUDA decode through this mode under the existing `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` flag. Supported inputs are BF16 QKV and norm weights, head dimensions 64/128/256, equal Q/K epsilon, and standard full-head NeoX rotary embeddings. The launcher validates layouts and devices before accessing pointers.
- Preserve the separate normalization/RoPE path for prefill, target verification, unsupported head dimensions/dtypes/rotary configurations, deterministic/on-policy configurations, and the prefill Inductor configuration. V and KV-cache writes are unchanged. No Q FP8 quantization is added.
- Add focused kernel and real-constructor/model-dispatch tests, including changing-input CUDA-graph replay. Two production files: +96/-15 lines; two test files: 259 lines.

## Accuracy Tests

Local validation on NVIDIA B200, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, CUDA 13.0:

### Post-merge correctness

Tested head: `9a11fd65f8a3e17dc9b476e9521c7668ac0a1ec2`, after merging main at `15d39bd8406bc75d2b1c82c5013cd0eb36368608`. All four PR files are byte-identical to feature commit `d79827f79cce6c110950c8265278031d5eec74b2`.

- **121 tests passed in 18.02 seconds**, with no failures/skips: 28 new kernel cases + 16 new model cases + 77 existing QK-norm/RoPE cases = 121. Existing suites used their CI-sized ranges. Coverage includes exact CUDA-reference comparisons, empty/padded rows, int32/int64 positions, long positions, exceptional values, preserved V/padding, invalid inputs, dispatch exclusions, and CUDA-graph replay.

### Additional pre-merge validation 

The results below were collected before the main merge, on the production code committed as `d79827f79c` with base `e22a530859`. These checks have not been repeated on `9a11fd65f8`:

- Negative controls caught both intentionally disabled CUDA-matching arithmetic and an intentionally disabled fused dispatch. These controls ran only in local subprocess memory.
- Additional numerical stress: 735 comparisons over 1,236,967,424 Q/K values, including repeated/replay comparisons. Zero bit mismatches for non-NaNs; NaN masks also matched. NaN payload bits are not part of the contract.
- Compute Sanitizer memcheck/synccheck reported zero errors; racecheck reported zero hazards.
- Live A/B: identical token IDs, text, logprobs, and top-5 results over 16,576 generated tokens. Another 192 fixed-prefix probes matched first-decode tokens/logprobs/top-20.
- Full GSM8K: **1,233/1,319 (93.480%) in both variants**, with all 1,319 generations identical and no request errors/truncations.

Run the focused and existing regression suites from the repository root in a compatible CUDA environment:

```bash
SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=1 SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=0 \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_table_qk_norm_rope.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_rope.py
```

These are local GPU results, not remote CI results. H100 remains untested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Historical, pre-merge measurements.** Baseline: `e22a53085994a68aaecbd7a109c8de6da32baeda`; fused production code matches feature commit `d79827f79cce6c110950c8265278031d5eec74b2`. The timings and profiles below have not been rerun on post-merge head `9a11fd65f8`. The 121-test post-merge pass above establishes focused correctness coverage, not a new performance result.

Same model revision, environment, flags, request shapes, and seed for the two measured variants:

- NVIDIA B200, TP1, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8@220b46e3b2180893580a4454f21f22d3ebb187d3`.
- FP8 weights with DeepGEMM; **BF16 activations and KV cache**; TRTLLM MHA.
- Decode CUDA graphs enabled; prefill CUDA graphs disabled.
- Eight fixed AB/BA pairs (16 fresh servers); 1,024 input / 512 output tokens at concurrency 1 and 32. Separate prefill requests used 1,024 input / 1 output token.
- Decode metric: window median first-to-last-token latency divided by 511. Reported latencies are geometric means of window medians; confidence intervals use paired log ratios across the eight pairs, not individual requests as independent repetitions.
- Quality evaluation and profiling were outside timing windows. No trials were dropped. All 10,752 measured requests completed without errors or prefix-cache hits.

Positive reduction means faster:

| Workload | Baseline | Fused (pre-merge) | Latency reduction | Paired 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Decode C1 TPOT | 2.93553 ms | 2.88372 ms | 1.765% | [1.760%, 1.769%] |
| Decode C32 TPOT | 4.31376 ms | 4.27861 ms | 0.815% | [0.636%, 0.993%] |
| Prefill C1 TTFT | 33.83691 ms | 34.34494 ms | -1.501% | [-3.343%, 0.307%] |
| Prefill C32 TTFT | 322.42732 ms | 321.96311 ms | 0.144% | [-0.321%, 0.607%] |

Decode improved in all eight pairs at both concurrency levels. These results apply to this machine/model/backend configuration, not all supported deployments.

**Prefill caveat:** the C1 interval does not establish neutrality or meet a 1% non-regression guardrail. A separate 40-block, same-resident eager-prefill control measured C1 slowdown of 0.189% with a 95% interval of [-2.698%, 3.160%]; its A/A control was also noisy. C32 passed the 1% guardrail. The follow-up measures synchronized `bench_one_batch.extend`, not HTTP TTFT, and does not prove that the observed HTTP slowdown is unrelated to this change.

Profiler engagement checks:

- Prefill: both variants launch 288 separate QK-norm and 288 separate RoPE kernels, no combined kernels, and 4,968 total kernel events.
- One initial prefill plus eight decode steps: baseline has 324 norm + 324 RoPE launches; this change has 36 norm + 36 RoPE launches for prefill and 288 combined decode launches. Total kernel events fall from 4,813 to 4,525: **36 fewer launches per decode step**. KV writes remain separate.

Server configuration used in both variants:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 \
  --revision 220b46e3b2180893580a4454f21f22d3ebb187d3 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tp-size 1 \
  --fp8-gemm-backend deep_gemm --attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.3 --random-seed 42 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30119 \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Run the full repository pre-commit suite. Ruff, Ruff format, isort, test-registry/entrypoint checks, and `git diff --check` passed locally; the complete pre-commit suite has not run.
- [x] Add focused unit/kernel regression tests.
- [ ] Update documentation if requested; this reuses an existing flag and operator.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results, including the unresolved prefill caveat.
- [x] Follow existing SGLang code/test conventions.
- [ ] Investigate the failed CI run badges and obtain green required checks; resolve the C1 prefill non-regression uncertainty before claiming blanket merge readiness.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: HunyuanImage-3 prefix K/V cache, opt-in FA3 attention and think-prompt support
issues.body:
## Motivation

Depends on #46600 (the CUDA MoE noise fix, which fixes #46461). This PR will be rebased on it once it lands, so the fix commit below will drop out of the diff.

Changes for HunyuanImage-3 (the prefix K/V cache is the main one; the opt-in FA3 attention and the `cot_text` fix are described under Modifications):

1. **Fix: generation on CUDA produced a noise texture** (on main too). The MoE block ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP read the expert output instead of the layer input and every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it; the cookbook also marks the CUDA recipe as unverified. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.
2. **Perf: cache the text prefix K/V across denoising steps.** HunyuanImage-3 recomputes the whole text prefix through every layer (attention and MoE) on every step, even though that prefix never changes. The proposal this implements:

> **P1. Prefix KV cache** (`hunyuan_image3.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager`, `forward_block`)
> The text prefix is causal and step-invariant. At `first_step`, keep the per-layer prefix K/V; on later steps feed only the image tokens as queries and attend to [cached prefix K/V, image K/V]. Replace the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA with FA varlen (prefix causal + image full) or flex.
> Removes L_text/(L_text+L_img) of the MoE compute per step. Large for long or "think" prompts; also recovers FlashAttention.

This PR does the prefix K/V cache with the dense SDPA as the default, plus the FA varlen part as an opt-in (`--attention-backend fa3`), since FA3 is not bitwise equal to SDPA. The official model does the same caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache).

## Modifications

**Fix (commit 2)**
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` runs the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
- `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: match the official `FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler` schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time; for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.

**Prefix K/V cache (commit 1)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager` stores each layer's prefix K/V on step 0, keyed by a cache slot, and on later steps prepends it to the suffix K/V. Adds `split_suffix_inputs` and `pad_prefix_rows`.
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `forward_block` takes `prefix_len` and `cache_slot`. Step 0 runs the full sequence; later steps run only the suffix rows and pad the output back to full length, so callers see the same shape.
- `ar_stage.py`: computes the prefix once as the rows before the first noisy-image or timestep token, and returns no prefix (full compute) when a clean image block straddles that boundary. `first_step` is now `step_idx == 0` (it was always `True`, and nothing read it). CFG cond and uncond use separate cache slots, since they run as two backbone calls on the same modules.
- Falls back to the current path when CLA is on, when the cache-dit adapter drives the blocks, or when no safe prefix exists.

Why the cache is exact: the mask is causal, so every row before the first varying token only sees prompt and clean conditioning tokens. Clean conditioning images before the noisy block are cached too, so the saving is a bit larger than L_text/(L_text+L_img).

Memory cost of the cache: `bs x P x kv_heads x head_dim x 4 bytes` per layer per CFG slot. Measured 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots (exactly the formula); the reported peak is unchanged.

**Opt-in FA3 segment attention (`--attention-backend fa3`)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `build_attention_segments` splits the mask (causal text, bidirectional image blocks) into `(start, end, causal)` segments; `segmented_attention` runs one FA3 varlen call per segment with bottom-right causal alignment, for both full and cached-suffix steps. GQA is native, so no `repeat_kv`. Hopper only; elsewhere the masked SDPA path is kept.
- `ar_stage.py` / `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: segments are built only when `attention_backend == "fa"` (what `fa3`/`fa4` resolve to). The default path is unchanged and still bitwise identical to main + fix.
- 2x H200: 22.6 s vs 26.8 s for the default path (1.55x vs main + fix). Not bitwise: PSNR 21-24 dB vs SDPA, same composition. On GPU the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly over 384 calls and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most one bf16 ulp per call, so the drift is kernel rounding compounding over layers and steps. Details and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422227024

**Fix: `cot_text` from the image API**
- `configs/sample/hunyuan_image3.py`: declare `bot_task`, `system_prompt` and `cot_text` in `image_request_extra_fields`. The image endpoint only forwards declared fields, so think/recaption text was silently dropped. With it, think prompts are 1.32x to 1.50x faster than main + fix (the reasoning text lands in the cached prefix), outputs identical: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422648092

## How the noise bug was found

On 2x H200 TP2 with debug-only instrumentation (not in this PR):
- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint. 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything feeding the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU unit tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`, all 11 in the file pass:
- Fix regressions: the shared MLP sees the layer input when the experts run in place; timesteps follow the official schedule. With only the two fixed source files reverted, exactly these two fail.
- Prefix cache: a cached suffix-only step matches full recompute; CFG slots do not overwrite each other; the prefix ends at the first varying token and is `None` when a clean image block straddles it.
- FA3 segments: segment attention equals masked SDPA for full and suffix-only steps; overlapping blocks fall back.
- Image API: `cot_text` and `bot_task` reach the sampling params.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

main + the fix vs this PR (prefix cache + fix), 2x H200 TP2 per the cookbook recipe, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 2.5, seed 42. One warmup then one timed request per prompt.

| | main + fix | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| short prompt, request | 34.97 s | 27.42 s | -21.6% (1.28x) |
| short prompt, AR/denoise stage | 34.19 s | 26.68 s | -22.0% |
| long prompt, request | 35.84 s | 27.49 s | -23.3% (1.30x) |
| long prompt, AR/denoise stage | 35.04 s | 26.75 s | -23.7% |
| peak memory (server log) | 106,318 MB | 106,318 MB | no change |
| output vs main + fix | | byte-identical on both prompts | PSNR inf |

Images and notes are in the results comment. Earlier numbers and the noise-texture images in older comments were taken before the fix and should be ignored.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit hooks (ruff F401/F821/F823/UP037, ruff-format)
- [x] Unit tests added (fix regressions + prefix cache)
- [x] GPU time / memory / parity on the fixed code
- [ ] Docs / cookbook update (the CUDA recipe could move from unverified once the numbers are in)

issues.title: [Feat] comfyui: Opt-in native worker batching (Z-Image, FLUX.1)
issues.body:
Refs #43411 (first model; the RFC stays open for the rest)

## Summary

ComfyUI calls the DiT with CFG cond/uncond (and `batch_size` > 1) as one batch. Since #43492 the executor sends one worker request per row. This adds opt-in batching, following the maintainer suggestion on the issue: per-row stays the default, batching is a user option, and it is only allowed for models checked against the per-row output.

- New `SGLDOptions.native_batching`: `off` (default, unchanged per-row path), `cfg_only` (one request per image holding its cond/uncond rows, so memory grows with CFG but not with `batch_size`), or `full` (one request for the whole batch).
- Each row's timestep goes in a new `Req.comfyui_row_timesteps` field; `req.timesteps` stays the one-step schedule the denoising loop walks. `DenoisingStage.expand_timestep_before_forward` uses the per-row timesteps instead of repeating one value.
- Out of memory: if the worker reports a CUDA OOM, the executor logs a warning and retries the step one mode lower (`full`, then `cfg_only`, then per-row) and stays there for the rest of the sampler run. A new run tries the chosen mode again. An OOM on the per-row path is raised as before.
- Per-row fields must have exactly B rows, and `cfg_only` needs ComfyUI's `cond_or_uncond` to find the chunks. Anything that does not match is rejected with a clear error, never split by guessing.
- `native_batching` other than `off` is refused at load time for models that are not verified and for more than one GPU. Verified so far: `lumina2` (Z-Image) and `flux` (FLUX.1, checked with FLUX.1-schnell).
- Z-Image adapter: keeps the `[B, L, D]` context and sends one text length per row (ComfyUI gives every row the same context length, same as the per-row path).
- Flux adapter: sends one CLIP and one T5 length per row (the worker checks them against the batch size). The worker takes one guidance value per request, so Flux rows with different guidance values are refused in a batch with a clear error; the per-row path still sends each row's own guidance.

## Tests

`test/unit/test_comfyui_native_batching.py` (new, 20 tests, CPU): Flux batch sends one text length per row and keeps row order; Flux rows with different guidance are refused when batched and keep their own guidance per-row; `full` is one request with per-row timesteps in order; `cfg_only` is one request per image with that image's cond and uncond rows, timesteps and options, and rows come back in ComfyUI's order; `cfg_only` with one image is one request; `cfg_only` without the cond chunks is rejected; OOM steps `full` down to `cfg_only`, or to per-row, stays there for the run and resets on the next run; OOM on the per-row path is raised; worker OOM errors are recognised and other errors are not; default still one request per row; batch of one unchanged; mismatched rows rejected; worker per-row timesteps; unverified models, multi-GPU and unknown modes refused; options node default. The rest of `test/unit/test_comfyui_*.py` passes unchanged (the 2 `test_comfyui_profile.py` failures also happen on main in my CPU environment, missing `uvicorn`). ruff, isort and codespell are clean.

## GPU check: Z-Image

Real SGLD worker in ComfyUI mode with Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo on one L40S, driven through the real `ZImageExecutor` with ComfyUI-shaped inputs (bf16 latents and context, fp32 timesteps, random tensors; only ComfyUI itself is left out).

### Memory and speed per mode

`batch_size` 2 with CFG (4 rows). Peak GPU memory while sampling; the weights take 13.8 GiB, so the extra column is the activation memory. Modes ran smallest first.

| | worker calls / step | peak GiB | extra over weights | ms / step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024px, off | 4 | 14.46 | 0.64 | 1167 |
| 1024px, cfg_only | 2 | 15.33 | 1.51 | 1219 |
| 1024px, full | 1 | 16.83 | 3.01 | 1269 |
| 2048px, off | 4 | 16.75 | 2.93 | 6842 |
| 2048px, cfg_only | 2 | 19.53 | 5.71 | 7152 |
| 2048px, full | 1 | 25.54 | 11.72 | 7196 |

At 2048px `cfg_only` takes about 2x the per-row activation memory and `full` about 4x, as expected for CFG and for `batch_size` 2 on top of it. At 1024px the per-row figure is small enough that the ratios are rough.

Earlier runs at other sizes (ms per step, `full` vs per-row):

| | per-row | full |
|---|---|---|
| 512px, B=2 | 155 | 142 (8% faster) |
| 512px, B=4 | 312 | 284 (9% faster) |
| 1024px, B=2 | 600 | 629 (5% slower) |
| 1024px, B=4 | 1220 | 1305 (7% slower) |

Batching helps when one row does not fill the GPU and costs a little at 1024px and above on an L40S, which is another reason to keep it opt-in.

### Out-of-memory fallback

Fresh worker, 2048px, 4 rows. After a per-row step, the test process filled the GPU until 4.2 GiB was free (per-row needs 2.8 GiB on top of the weights), then ran a step with `full`:

- `full` ran out of memory, `cfg_only` ran out of memory, and the step finished per-row. Two warnings were logged: `...native_batching=full; using cfg_only...` and `...native_batching=cfg_only; using off...`.
- The result matched the per-row output exactly (relative L2 0.0). That step made 6 worker calls (the 2 failed attempts plus 4 per-row).
- The next step in the same run went straight to per-row (4 calls).
- After freeing the memory, a new run with `full` made 1 call again.

The worker kept running after both OOMs.

### Accuracy

Per-row reruns are bit identical. Relative L2 against the per-row output; the right column nudges the per-row inputs by about one bf16 rounding step (2^-8 relative) to show the noise level:

| case | batched vs per-row | nudged per-row vs per-row |
|---|---|---|
| CFG pair, B=2, 1024px (full) | 3.7% | 6.3% |
| per-row timesteps, B=3, 1024px (full) | 3.3% | 9.3% |
| batch 2 x CFG, B=4, 1024px (full) | 3.2% | 4.6% |
| 8-step Euler trajectory, B=2 (full) | 19.6% | 19.0% |
| B=4, 1024px, cfg_only / full | 3.07% / 3.06% | |
| B=4, 2048px, cfg_only / full | 3.00% / 3.00% | |

So the batched vs per-row gap is within bf16 noise for this model on these inputs. With two identical rows in one batch, the two outputs are bit identical (max abs 0.0), so rows do not leak into each other; the gap is the bf16 kernels rounding differently at another batch size. An fp32 reference was not possible: the fused RoPE kernel (`apply_rope_pos_ids_cos_sin_cache`) only dispatches half types.

Each row uses its own timestep: in a batch with timesteps 0.9 / 0.5 / 0.1, each batched row is 0.4 to 0.9 max abs from a single-row call at its own timestep and 4.7 to 6.4 from a call at a different timestep.

## GPU check: FLUX.1-schnell

Same setup with black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell through the real `FluxExecutor` (T5 context 256 tokens, pooled CLIP vector, random tensors) on one L40S.

Memory and speed, `batch_size` 2 with CFG (4 rows); the weights take 24.1 GiB:

| | worker calls / step | extra over weights | ms / step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512px, off | 4 | 0.28 GiB | 432 |
| 512px, cfg_only | 2 | 0.46 GiB | 407 (6% faster) |
| 512px, full | 1 | 0.82 GiB | 394 (9% faster) |
| 1024px, off | 4 | 0.84 GiB | 1450 |
| 1024px, cfg_only | 2 | 1.48 GiB | 1514 (4% slower) |
| 1024px, full | 1 | 2.69 GiB | 1575 (9% slower) |

Accuracy at 1024px (relative L2 against per-row; per-row reruns are bit identical; nudged = per-row inputs nudged by about one bf16 rounding step):

| case | batched vs per-row | nudged per-row vs per-row |
|---|---|---|
| CFG pair, B=2 (full) | 0.25% | 0.33% |
| batch 2 x CFG, B=4 (full / cfg_only) | 0.26% / 0.26% | 1.02% |
| per-row timesteps 0.9 / 0.5 / 0.1, B=3 (full) | 0.29% | 0.91% |
| duplicate rows, B=2 (full) | 0.26% | 0.52% |
| 4-step Euler trajectory, B=2 (full) | 0.13% | 0.40% |

- Duplicate rows in one batch give bit identical outputs (max abs 0.0).
- Each row uses its own timestep: against a single-row call, max abs 0.25 to 1.0 at its own timestep and about 4.0 at another one.
- One row looked off at first: the t=0.9 row of the 0.9 / 0.5 / 0.1 batch is 4.1% from per-row while the others are about 0.27%. That row's output is small (norm 582 vs 8,814 and 38,297), and nudging the per-row inputs moves that same row by 10% to 15% (3 seeds), so it is within noise. With both rows at t=0.9 the gap is 0.27% vs 0.5% to 0.95% for the nudge.

FLUX.1-dev uses the same DiT plus a guidance embedding, which gets one value per request; batches with mixed guidance are refused as above.

## Limitations

- Verified on one GPU for Z-Image and FLUX.1-schnell only; other models get a clear error unless `native_batching` is `off`. Each further model needs its own GPU comparison against per-row output. FLUX.1-dev was not run separately.
- Inputs were random tensors, not real prompts.
- Reference-latent and ControlNet rows do not apply to Z-Image, so they are not covered here.
- The OOM fallback depends on the worker reporting the error text "out of memory"; a hard crash of the worker process is not recovered by it.

## Motivation

In Kimi-K2.5 MXFP4 decode on ROCm gfx95, the absorbed MLA value projection is a batched A16W4 GEMM that writes a BF16 tensor, and `o_proj` immediately quantizes it back to MXFP4. Doing the quantization in the GEMM epilogue skips that HBM round trip and one launch.

Independent of #32935 (key projection + RoPE + KV-cache write fusion); this branch is based on `main`.

## Modifications

- New Triton kernel `batched_gemm_a16wfp4_flatten_mxfp4_quant` in `sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.mla_value_bmm_mxfp4_hip`, registered as `gemm.batched_gemm_a16wfp4_flatten_mxfp4_quant` (Triton, HIP). It keeps the split path's BF16 rounding point, so values and scales match it bit for bit.
- AITER decode uses it when `w_vc` and `o_proj` are MXFP4. Switch `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FUSE_MLA_VALUE_MXFP4_QUANT`, on by default.
- Shapes, dtypes or AITER configs it does not support fall back to the split GEMM + `fused_flatten_mxfp4_quant`. DSA and LoRA on `kv_b_proj` keep the split path.

issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] minimax: gfx950 sparse attention, NVFP4 KV and DSpark verify kernels
issues.body:
> Part of the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash AMD series that replaces #45936 (closed with its base branch `minimax-m3.1-flash`): kernel PRs #46690 (attention), #46691 (MoE / GEMM) and #46692 (quick all-reduce), each on `main`; then #46693 with the M3.1 call sites and #46694 (indexer CP). It follows the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD layout (#41018-#41021, then #41308).

## Summary
- **NVFP4 KV (MSA-v1 layout).** `minimax_sparse/common/nvfp4.py` reads the packed rows for the Triton kernels and `nvfp4_gfx950.py` dequantizes them in Gluon. The kernel tests build their packed caches with a torch quantizer in `NVFP4KVQuantizeUtil`'s layout (`nvfp4_kv_quantize` in `sglang/test/quant_ref_utils.py`).
- **Sparse decode.** `decode/nvfp4_decode_gfx950.py` runs sparse decode over the packed NVFP4 K/V in Gluon (one program per row, top-k chunk and KV head; per-warp online softmax). `decode/nvfp4_decode.py` holds the NVFP4 verify scorer; `topk_sparse.py` dispatches an `Nvfp4Cache` to it.
- **Verify indexer.** `decode/verify_topk_idx.py` scores a linear draft chain against one shared prefix; `decode/verify_topk_gfx950.py` fuses the per-block max score with a streaming top-k on MFMA tiles.
- **Prefill.** `prefill/index_topk_gfx950.py` is the fused prefill indexer; `prefill/gluon_prefill_pair_gfx950.py` runs two queries per program over the union of their top-k blocks; `prefill/nvfp4_prefill.py` gathers the NVFP4 cache into the Gluon prefill's paged layout; `prefill/gluon_prefill.py` and `prefill/flash_with_topk_idx.py` take the new cache.
- **fp8 O epilogue.** `common/out_quant_gfx950.py` is shared by the Gluon decode and pair prefill: they can write O directly as the fp8 o_proj input, with the same bytes and scales as aiter's separate per-token or 1x128 quant.
- **QK-norm + RoPE.** `minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope.py` adds the gfx950 fused Gemma Q/K RMSNorm + partial RoPE + KV-cache write.
- **HiCache.** The NVFP4 page-row copy takes its CTA quota as a template argument: 32 on HIP (MI350X needs 16+ to saturate PCIe), 2 on CUDA as before.
- **Verify MLA.** `verify_mla.py` lets the gfx950 grouped-head split-KV verify serve the DSpark draft's sliding window (its non-causal draft block, window 4095); `num_stages=2` was 13-26% faster for that window.
- The M3.1 call sites (NVFP4 pool, verify indexer, fp8 O for `o_proj`, windowed draft verify) are in the integration PR.

## Serving gain of each kernel
Measured in the integration PR at TP4 on MI350X (NVFP4 KV, DSpark acceptance simulated at 3 tokens per step, 32K-token contexts), each change turned off alone; the share decode TPOT or prefill latency grows without it, mean of two GPU sets:
- Windowed draft verify (`verify_mla`): decode TPOT +20.6% at 1 request, +8.2-9.6% at 8-64.
- Two-queries-per-program Gluon prefill (`gluon_prefill_pair_gfx950`): 32K-token prefill +10.3%, decode +4.2-5.4% at 8-64.
- Gluon prefill over an FP8 KV pool (`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_AMD_KV_FORMAT=fp8`): prefill +11.7% (32K tokens) and +12.4% (eight 8K requests).
- NVFP4 KV itself (kernel level, CUDA-graph replay, per layer): the verify indexer at 110K context takes 0.75-0.84x FP8's time from 8 requests and sparse decode 0.42-0.68x, with 1.78x the tokens per GB of KV.

## Changes to existing kernels
On CUDA nothing changes: `topk_sparse` only dispatches the new `Nvfp4Cache` type, the decode top-k only moves into `select_decode_topk`, and the page-row quota stays 2.

On gfx950, main's MiniMax-M3 layers switch kernels when this merges, with no new call site:
- QK-norm + RoPE + cache store (`sparse_qk_index_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_cache`) runs the tiled kernel for M3's 128-wide head with 64-dim neox RoPE; its bf16 outputs equal the per-head kernel's bit for bit.
- The Gluon sparse prefill pairs two queries per program for bf16 batches from 2048 tokens (16 query heads), and now also serves an fp8 KV pool at its per-tensor k/v scales, which `minimax_sparse_prefill` now passes on; before, an fp8 pool stayed on Triton. Both match the Triton kernel up to bf16 rounding.
- The prefill indexer uses the fused gfx950 index top-k for score-only max layers at unit scales and 128-aligned pages; on these bf16 / fp8 index caches it emits the Triton two-pass indexer's block ids exactly. It keeps Triton when Gluon's CDNA4 module is missing.

On other ROCm GPUs, the per-head QK-norm kernel, which serves them (and gfx950 heads other than M3's), no longer writes main K/V to slot 0, the reserved CUDA-graph padding slot. The unfused `store_cache` already skips it, and no real token is stored there.

## Verification
- MI350X (ROCm 7.2 image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`, AITER `acf8fdf93`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), this branch alone on `main`: `test_minimax_gfx950_prefill` 35 passed, `test_minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope` 55, `test_minimax_nvfp4_sparse_decode` 13, `test_minimax_verify_topk_idx` 68 (the kernel cases; the integration PR adds 8 more), `test_verify_shared_kv` 10. pre-commit clean; main's callers of every modified kernel module import.
- Not executed on this branch alone: CUDA (shared files keep main's behavior there), end-to-end serving.

issues.title: [Perf] MOSS-Image: Fuse joint-block QKV projections in high quality
issues.body:
## Motivation

MOSS-Image joint blocks run three separate Q/K/V GEMMs for every conditional and unconditional denoising pass. This PR packs those projections for `quality=high` and lets the existing ordered RMSNorm+RoPE kernel read their strided Q/K views directly. The latter avoids copying Q and K back to contiguous storage after each packed GEMM.

The measured scope is MOSS-Image-Base, 1024×1024, 50 steps, batch 1 / concurrency 1 on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Four repeated temporal pairs give a geometric-mean E2E speedup of **1.0141× over main** (1.386% lower latency) and **1.0222× over native Omni**; every pair is faster. The primary timed input is the fixed short product-photograph prompt; the long and Chinese prompts are quality checks. This is an eager optimization; it does not add or claim BCG coverage.

- Frozen main baseline: `af21e2b989e482cfdce39689126562f2209d53ac`.
- Tested PR head: `d752066eaa6f5091fa4c8daa2ba1d5d43a3928cd`.
- Native vLLM-Omni comparator: `817d4c17feb702289a2d2b2cbacfd594c262b7a7`.
- Common checkpoint: `OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image-Base@85975793d8b3d432f1b6e27f352abaa4c2a4c0d3`; all downloaded files were verified against the pinned file hashes.

## Modifications

- Reuse the existing checkpoint name mapping to merge Q/K/V in that order into one weight. There is no duplicate model weight or persistent view cache.
- Pass the quality choice through the request's denoising branch. `high` uses one packed GEMM; `exact/lossless` use three separate `F.linear` calls with fresh slices of the packed weight. A later request can change quality without reloading weights or mutating a module-wide mode.
- Extend the existing ordered norm+RoPE kernel to accept contiguous heads with a regular token stride. Reduction order and BF16 rounding in this kernel are unchanged; its result remains contiguous. Other layouts keep the existing fallback.
- Extend existing loading-order, quality-dispatch, offload/stream and numerical/stride tests; document the quality policy in the existing MOSS cookbook.

## Accuracy Tests

A wider GEMM changes BF16 rounding. The first unconditional version failed the task's lossless byte-exact gate, so packing is explicitly restricted to `high`.

Final committed-head serving checks under the selected cuDNN configuration pass: all three lossless prompt outputs match actual main lossless byte for byte, both before and after high requests. Each short → long → Chinese → short sequence also repeats the first PNG exactly. Final main/PR high outputs match their respective paired-benchmark outputs; collecting a Torch profile preserves the same high PNG.

High-quality main/PR comparison, using the actual final-head outputs shown below:

| Prompt | SSIM | PSNR (dB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Short product photograph | 0.993826 | 38.0795 |
| Long still life, worst main/PR sample | 0.971474 | 32.2421 |
| Chinese café poster | 0.996791 | 37.7274 |

The task's predeclared image-alignment thresholds are SSIM ≥ 0.95 and PSNR ≥ 28 dB. These are numeric alignment gates, supplemented by visual inspection, not a broad perceptual-equivalence study. The long sample preserves a baseline prompt mismatch: both show two visible pears although the prompt asks for three. Short → long → Chinese → short checks repeat the first PNG exactly within each process. All 12 process-level quality gates passed. Within each arm, all three prompt PNGs are also identical across its four restarts. Across all main/candidate/Omni reference checks, the lowest SSIM is 0.969576 and lowest PSNR is 28.4811 dB (main vs Omni). Candidate vs matched main has the per-prompt metrics above; candidate vs Omni has minimum SSIM 0.985401 and PSNR 28.5654 dB.

All figures below paste the complete source PNGs at their original pixel scale, with labels outside image bounds. Both sides use seed 1101, 1024×1024, 50 steps, CFG 3, flow shift 5, skip layer 22 / SLG window 0.01–1.0, BF16 DiT/text encoder, FP32 VAE/solver, high quality and transformer cuDNN SDPA.

![Actual main and PR short-prompt outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8df03e213fe39d57c723da266338b5236674f144/00-image-short-main-vs-pr.png)

![Actual main and PR long-prompt outputs, worst paired quality sample](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8df03e213fe39d57c723da266338b5236674f144/01-image-long-main-vs-pr.png)

![Actual main and PR Chinese-poster outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/8df03e213fe39d57c723da266338b5236674f144/02-image-text-main-vs-pr.png)

Exact prompts and media hashes: [evidence branch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/bbuf/rtx6000-diffusion-20261026-moss-qkv-evidence).

Validation executed on the actual SM120 GPU after cleanup:

- Existing MOSS norm tests: 30 passed, including packed nonzero offsets, batch/odd sequence lengths, extreme values and rejected strides.
- MOSS model and CPU-distributed tests: 115 passed, including loading order, quality dispatch and high/separate projection offload with alternate streams. The CPU-distributed tests do not establish GPU multicard performance.
- Repository-selected Ruff rules, Ruff formatting and isort passed; `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Arm | Denoise p50 (s) | HTTP E2E p50 / p95 (s) | Sequential requests/s | Peak NVML (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGL main, eager high + cuDNN | 14.5002 | 14.7131 / 14.7194 | 0.067966 | 32.2065 |
| PR final head, eager high + cuDNN | 14.2931 | 14.5095 / 14.5145 | 0.068920 | 32.2787 |
| Native Omni, regional compile + cuDNN | 14.4178† | 14.8269 / 14.8480 | 0.067423 | 32.5034 |

PR peak NVML memory is **74 MiB higher than main**. The primary E2E results contain 16 measured requests from four processes per arm. Per-process measured CV ranges are main 0.00768–0.03252%, PR 0.01970–0.03256%, Omni 0.01309–0.04414%.

| Temporal pair | Main / PR | Omni / PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cycle 1 forward | 1.013838× | 1.022582× |
| Cycle 1 reverse | 1.014105× | 1.021613× |
| Cycle 2 forward | 1.014191× | 1.021622× |
| Cycle 2 reverse | 1.014079× | 1.023077× |
| Geometric mean | **1.014053×** | **1.022223×** |

Process launch-to-ready ranges: main 56.04–56.05 s, PR 54.05–56.05 s, Omni 32.02 s, observed with 2-second readiness polling. Eight additional thermal-warmup requests take 117.41–117.55 s / 115.83–115.87 s / 118.39–118.49 s respectively. Compiler/JIT caches are reused across process restarts; these are not isolated cold-compile estimates. BCG is disabled, with no new graph capture/replay claim.

The protocol runs two symmetric main / PR / Omni / Omni / PR / main cycles on the same physical GPU: four fresh processes and 16 measured requests per arm. Each process first passes the three-prompt and repeated-short quality gate, then runs eight thermal warmups and four timed requests. All rows, including failed configuration screens, are retained. GPU0 UUID and owned PIDs are checked in archived NVML samples; GPU1 remains idle. No Torch/Nsight profiler runs during these timings.

HTTP E2E covers submission through receipt of all response bytes; client PNG decoding/writing is outside the timer. Startup and warmups are reported separately. Launch-to-ready uses each framework's native readiness boundary: SGL includes its configured 50-step built-in warmup, while Omni's health readiness precedes the qualification requests. This is not a same-work cold-start comparison. Both then receive the same quality sequence and eight extra thermal warmups. SGL native stage timing is enabled equally for main and PR. Its denoise stage includes the scheduler. † Omni denoise-core p50 is **14.417836 s** across four separately instrumented requests. Its default profiler did not time the actual MOSS full-forward loop, so an isolated diagnostic checkout adds four lines configuring the existing native profiler targets: `predict_noise_with_slg`, `scheduler_step_maybe_with_cfg`, encoder and VAE. Logs verify exactly 50 prediction and 50 Euler calls per request, and their sums agree with response metrics. This boundary excludes the surrounding Python loop/setup, unlike the SGL denoise stage. The primary Omni checkout and all primary E2E timing rows are unchanged. No cross-framework denoise speedup is inferred from these different boundaries.

Both SGL arms use the faster qualified explicit transformer cuDNN configuration. Omni's native Blackwell default already selects `CUDNN_ATTN`; it keeps regional compilation enabled with `TORCHINDUCTOR_EMULATE_PRECISION_CASTS=1`. The default compile configuration without cast emulation failed the restart quality gate (PSNR 27.449 < 28), so its timing is not used as a qualified comparison. SGL MOSS rejects torch.compile in this pinned source.

Library stacks are native to each framework and disclosed rather than silently equated:

| Component | SGL main / PR | Omni |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PyTorch / CUDA wheel | 2.14.1+cu130 | 2.13.0+cu130 |
| Triton | 3.8.0 | 3.7.1 |
| cuDNN | 9.24.0.43 | 9.20.0.48 |
| Transformers | 5.19.0 | 5.19.0 |

Driver 595.84, stock 600 W power limit; one 97,887 MiB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Both use the same physical GPU, weights, input, seed, precision and generation contract. No quantization or offload is enabled in the measured cell.

Final-head cuDNN traces compare complete GPU `ProfilerStep#2/#3/#4` for the same short request. Average diagnostic values:

| Per denoising step | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU step annotation | 289.527 ms | 285.502 ms |

The earlier packed-only prototype's Torch-flash trace added 166 BF16 copies per step (~5.75 ms total copy time); the final implementation preserves main's nine small copies. The model-level paired result above is the net benefit. These independent traces are diagnostic, not latency benchmarks. Whole-trace kernel sums contain different work outside the matched annotations and are not compared as E2E time. Both final traces have zero CUDA-graph launches.

Cleanup removed an unused test allocation and added the quality-policy documentation; production code was unchanged from the validated strided version. Same-configuration before/after A/A p50: 14.684656 s → 14.682991 s (ratio 0.999887), with CV 0.03669% / 0.02480%; all repeated outputs were identical. Full diff was self-reviewed using BBuf cleanup source/review references [#39293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39293), [#42391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42391), and [#40265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40265).

Public response JSON omits repeated base64 PNG payloads; complete original responses, PNGs and server logs remain in the task archive. Profiling uses separate requests and does not contribute primary timing rows.

issues.title: [Feat] sglang-processor: GLM-5.3-Flash image preprocessing
issues.body:
Stacked on #46562. Co-authored with @ScarletGuo. Rebased with the stack onto `main` `911693e3f8`, which includes #45449. The two GLM commits applied unchanged.

Add GLM-5.3-Flash image preprocessing. Dynamo's `glm5_next` family plans tokens but does not process pixels. (A followup upstream PR is feasible).

## Modifications

- **`mm/models/glm5_next.rs`.** Ports SGLang's `Glm4vImageProcessor` and transformers' `Glm5NextImageProcessor` onto Dynamo's planner:
  - resize to the content size (no upscale above the token minimum), zero-pad to the canvas;
  - normalize and patchify in Qwen-VL's order;
  - glm4v image-only M-RoPE.

  Images decode as SGLang's `smart_to_rgb` does: EXIF transpose, then alpha (PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP with an alpha bitmask) composited onto an edge-contrasting background with PIL's `paste` rounding.
- **`MmPipelineSpec`.** Dynamo's `ProcessorSpec`, or a family spec carrying the knobs Dynamo's spec lacks: GLM's mean, std and resample. Decoding is chosen per family when the processor is built.
- **`RUST_MM_FAMILIES`.** Adds `glm5_next` through `Glm4vImageProcessor`, honoring `min_image_tokens` / `max_image_tokens` overrides.
- **`generate_mm_parity.py`.** Picks the processor class through SGLang's registry, and takes each family's image delimiters and overrides from a small table.

## Tests

- New fixture `mm_parity/glm-5.3-flash.json` (26 cases): every corpus format, the PIL backend, two images, and token overrides. All are bit-exact with Python's CPU path under Pillow 12.3, except the existing 16-bit `known_gap`. Disabling alpha compositing fails 7 of them.
- The corpus gains `rgba_bitfields_56x56.bmp`, a BITMAPV4 BMP with an alpha bitmask. Pillow opens it as RGBA, so `smart_to_rgb` composites it. Pillow can't write one (it saves RGBA as BI_RGB, which reads back as RGB), so the generator writes the header by hand.
- The Qwen fixtures' existing cases regenerate byte-identical. The Qwen2.5-VL format sweep gains this PR's three new corpus images.
- `test_rust_mm_gate` gains the GLM entry.
- At this head (`96a7f52353`): `cargo test -p sglang-processor --all-features`, including the GLM fixture, and `cargo test -p sglang-server` (388) pass. The Python `test/registered/unit/multimodal/rust/` tests pass, and clippy `-D warnings`, rustfmt and pre-commit are clean.
- Not run yet: an end-to-end GLM-5.3-Flash run (bit-exact `/generate`, MMMU / MMMU-Pro).

issues.title: [Feat] [NPU] speculative: support NGRAM decoding for MHA and MLA
issues.body:
## Motivation

NGRAM produces dynamic verification trees without a draft model. Ascend currently rejects its corpus options, and simply opening the device guard leaves tree attention, verification, and accepted KV relocation incomplete. This PR enables the complete path for full-attention MHA/GQA and dense MLA target models.

Kernel dependency: https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/854, now at `cd687d534fe10907f0ea1286ad8eff42c952107d`. It provides the dedicated `verify_ngram_tree_greedy` API and `mem_cache.mla_cache_move.move_mla_kv_cache`; the current framework requires these APIs. The earlier tested revision is recorded below. The reconstruction proposed in kernel PR #484 alone does not provide this serving path.

## Modifications

- Integrate current main kernel dispatch: NPU reconstruction now uses `sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.reconstruct_tree`, and NGRAM-only greedy verification is selected in `sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.spec_tree`. Keep the upstream CPU-mirror/mirrorless attention branches, while retaining the CPU mirror required by NGRAM FIA.
- Enable MHA/GQA NGRAM target-verification NPU graphs with a fixed-address, per-bucket FIA mask buffer. Refresh live tree masks, padding rows, and graph-bound KV lengths before replay. Honor `--disable-cuda-graph`; retain eager prefill and MLA. The graph runner changes are restricted to NGRAM, and the legacy MTP verifier remains unchanged.
- Isolate NPU greedy verification: `eagle_sample` passes an explicit `is_ngram` flag derived from `SpecInputType.NGRAM_VERIFY`; only that type lazily imports `sgl_kernel_npu.sample.verify_ngram_tree_greedy.verify_ngram_tree_greedy`. EAGLE/MTP and other types keep the existing `verify_tree_greedy` implementation and default dispatch.
- Reuse the existing shared CPU trie/SAM and CUDA/CPU configuration checks for all eight corpus options. NPU uses synchronous scheduling; MHA/GQA supports target-verification graphs, while prefill and MLA remain eager.
- Import `build_ngram_attention_mask` from `sgl_kernel_npu.attention.ngram_attention` only inside the NGRAM target-verification metadata branch. Both the builder and its Triton kernel live in the kernel repository; the Ascend backend retains no mask implementation or forwarding wrapper.
- Share `forward_mtp` between MTP and NGRAM verification and remove `forward_ngram`. Reuse KV writes, real-token/DP-padding handling, block tables, cache layouts, MLA latent/RoPE preparation, and FIA workspace/output dispatch. Select the NGRAM ancestor mask with sparse mode 0; retain the existing MTP mask/modes. MHA NGRAM retains BSH and per-request query lengths because paged TND split-fuse requires a causal mask; MLA shares TND with cumulative query lengths.
- Lazily call the kernel-repository MLA relocation helper for dense FP16/BF16 caches. Fuse the latent/RoPE source/target NZ index expansions into one Triton kernel; retain native gather snapshots before overlapping scatter writes across every layer. ND retains native row addressing. Keep the existing fallback for FP8 and indexed caches. Use a metadata-only BF16 payload view for FP16 relocation so native copies preserve all 16-bit patterns.
- Remove the blanket MLA rejection and consolidate the four NGRAM-specific backend error sites into two capability checks. Retain checks for unsupported attention/cache semantics and parallelism, including DCP, which requires local/global KV slot translation.
- Document the supported scope and add kernel-mask, MLA attention/cache, configuration, and real-model regressions.

Supported KV types are FP16/BF16; W8A8 target weights are independent of KV dtype. Sliding-window/linear attention, sparse indexed MLA, sinks, ALiBi, logit capping, PP/CP/DCP, and chain rejection sampling remain unsupported. The existing NGRAM DP-attention restriction remains in place.

## Accuracy Tests

**Shared-forward and MLA-index fusion update (2026-10-27):** framework `c24cba4c4aacba9a8fecfe33eb71338dbeec0b06` with kernel `cd687d534fe10907f0ea1286ad8eff42c952107d`, machine 151, Ascend910_9362, CANN 9.1 B083, TP=1.

- **111 related tests passed:** 39 shared CPU corpus checks, 8 NPU framework checks, 28 existing kernel checks, and 36 new relocation/index checks.
- Independent FP32 CPU attention oracles exercise both the original MTP causal path and NGRAM ancestor masks on NPU. MLA covers FP16/BF16, ND/NZ, 12-to-16 head padding, ragged prefixes, nonconsecutive pages, page-crossing drafts, and KV writes. MHA/GQA covers both tensor-bound eager lengths and graph-bound Python lengths. This is attention-path coverage, not an end-to-end MTP model test.
- **Qwen3-0.6B BF16 eager-versus-graph generation passed** after sharing the forward path. Capture buckets were 1/2/4; actual graph replay was observed at live batch sizes 1/2/3/4, including padded replay and the long-prefix case.
- New relocation checks compare raw 16-bit payloads, including NaN payloads and signed zeros, across overlap cycles, repeated sources, cross-page locations, empty inputs, and strided int32 locations. Additional boundary cases check int32 logical slots that expand beyond int32 NZ rows and int64 logical slots above 2^31. Power-of-two page addressing uses shifts/masks to avoid int32 division rounding near the slot limit.
- Profiling the 27-layer NZ/12-token move reduced **operator enqueues from 32 to 5** and **device tasks from 42 to 11**: one fused index kernel plus the two native gather/scatter pairs. Native index-copy still includes internal transpose tasks.
- Sixteen deployed source files matched the committed sources. Import sorting, Black/Ruff formatting and scoped lint, Python AST checks, and diff checks passed.

**Resource limitation:** the real DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 MLA rerun failed during weight loading, before attention or generation. An unrelated TP16 workload started on 151 at 22:49:12 and occupied approximately 55 GB on every chip. A 354 MiB allocation failed with 11.89 MiB free. The other workload was left running. MLA attention/cache unit checks passed, but this update does **not** claim a completed real MLA model rerun.

Paired old/new relocation microbenchmarks were collected for 27/61 layers, ND/NZ, and 1/3/8/12/32/64/128 moved tokens (10 warmups, median of five repeats of 100 synchronized calls). The final measurements overlapped that TP16 workload. They are preliminary contended measurements, not dedicated-device latency or end-to-end throughput evidence. No new performance chart is added; the earlier throughput section remains tied to its listed revisions. A dedicated-device performance rerun and real MLA model rerun remain outstanding.

**Conflict resolution verified on 2026-10-27:** commit `c426f1f7cbb2cd416c3ca48c7b58da30498354e7` merges main `7fe5b127e4ac2a3b2c67e1bc1fb2a299daf0983e`. GitHub reports the PR as **MERGEABLE**. Validation used kernel commit `ffe740d07db9e2e02f3dc195ba3780df7ac3ddd0` on machine 151, Qwen3-0.6B BF16, TP=1, CANN 9.1 B083. The committed Git tree exactly matches the tested tree; twelve runtime source files were checked against the deployed sources.

- **72 related pytest cases passed**, with two MLA tests deselected. Coverage includes the shared corpus checks, NPU MHA/configuration/KV metadata checks, and kernel regressions.
- **Four dispatch checks passed** after migrating to the upstream kernel entry points: NGRAM selects its dedicated verifier; other verification types retain the legacy verifier.
- **All eight corpus-option cases passed:** 2,304 greedy token IDs matched the ordinary baseline, and all eight stochastic option cases completed.
- The registered long-prefix **NGRAM eager-versus-graph regression passed**, with target-verification capture buckets 1/2/4 and actual graph replay at live batch sizes 1/2/3/4, including padded replay.
- With `SGLANG_NPU_ATTN_BACKEND_NEEDS_CPU_SEQ_LENS=0` and `ASCEND_USE_FIA=false`, NGRAM retained its required host mirror, captured/replayed a graph, and generated 96 tokens in a targeted smoke test.
- The initial graph attempt could not import `acl` because the standalone harness had replaced the container's CANN `PYTHONPATH`. Restoring the container CANN Python path resolved the environment issue; the affected graph regression was rerun successfully.
- Import sorting, Ruff formatting/lint, `git diff --check`, and **Mintlify build validation passed**. The site-wide broken-link scan reports 819 links across 254 files: 253 reported source files are unchanged from main, and the reported cookbook anchor in the one changed page already exists on main. No unrelated documentation links were changed for this merge.

This rerun covers MHA/GQA. MLA model runs, end-to-end MTP model tests, GSM8K accuracy, and throughput were not rerun. Earlier results below remain historical results for their listed revisions.

**Earlier graph-support commit: `ba7f555cd235f75038b56ad431e6b660550f1ed6` (2026-10-27).** This commit turns the earlier MHA graph experiment into production code, removes its replay trace instrumentation, gates graph support to MHA/GQA, and updates configuration, metadata, long-prefix generation tests, and documentation. The user requested submission before further test runs; the final end-to-end rerun and documentation build validation were stopped, so this commit does not claim a completed full regression run. Five scoped MHA/configuration/KV checks passed during preparation. Import sorting, Ruff formatting/lint, and `git diff --check` passed.

Before this production commit, the isolated experiment on machine 151 used Qwen3-0.6B BF16, TP=1, CANN 9.1 B083, framework base `6ecd79edb80407dbe84e5476214be8c1366fc3fb`, and kernel `ffe740d07db9e2e02f3dc195ba3780df7ac3ddd0`. It completed **102 actual NPUGraph replays** and matched NGRAM eager for **912 greedy token IDs and their returned log probabilities**, including capture buckets 1/2/4, real batch 3 padded to 4, and KV lengths up to 291. A separate full-mask FIA probe matched eager across four replays that changed prefix lengths and tree topology. These are experimental results preceding the production commit, not a test result for its final source. MLA graphs, overlap scheduling, multi-device TP, GSM8K accuracy, and throughput were not rerun.

**Earlier isolation validation on 2026-10-20 (MHA/GQA only):** framework `6ecd79edb80407dbe84e5476214be8c1366fc3fb` with kernel `ffe740d07db9e2e02f3dc195ba3780df7ac3ddd0`, machine 151, Ascend910, CANN 9.1 B083, Qwen3-0.6B BF16, TP=1. This model has 16 query heads and 8 KV heads.

- **32 tests passed:** 28 kernel tests plus 4 MHA/configuration/KV tests. The two MLA tests were deselected.
- **Four dispatch checks passed:** only `NGRAM_VERIFY` selects `verify_ngram_tree_greedy`; EAGLE verification retains the legacy verifier for top-k 1, -1, and 4. These are dispatch checks, not end-to-end MTP model tests.
- **All eight corpus-option cases passed:** 2,304 greedy token IDs matched the non-speculative FIA baseline, including the second batch that reuses the online trie. Eight stochastic cases also completed at temperature 0.7, top-k 10, top-p 0.9, with 24 tokens each.
- Default NGRAM and root-only each matched another 288 greedy token IDs: **2,880 compared greedy tokens in total**. The maximum observed log-probability difference in the eight-option matrix was 0.0801032; token IDs matched.
- Nine deployed runtime files were verified against the current PR sources. The restored legacy verifier is unchanged from before this PR.
- The external validation helper initially assumed root-only responses include `spec_accept_length`. Collection was corrected to treat that metric as optional, and root-only was rerun successfully. Repository code did not change.

MLA, end-to-end MTP models, GSM8K accuracy, and throughput were not rerun for this isolation update. Earlier results below remain tied to their explicitly listed revisions.

Machine 151, Linux, Ascend910_9362, CANN 9.1 B083, TP=1. Framework commit `4ec6cbf704a02e654f67c9e0131c2884f4a402b2` and companion kernel commit `674b503190c98c4114fa6c26806d36824cb736aa` were tested together.

- **78 regressions passed:** 44 shared CPU corpus tests, 6 NPU framework tests, and 28 kernel tests.
- **Qwen3-0.6B BF16:** all eight corpus-option variants matched the non-speculative baseline for **2,304 greedy tokens**.
- **DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8, BF16 KV:** all eight variants matched the FIA non-speculative baseline for **2,304 greedy tokens**.
- Both matrices also completed eight stochastic cases each, with temperature 0.7, top-k 10, top-p 0.9, and 24 tokens.
- MLA default and root-only generation each matched the corresponding baseline for 288 tokens in **both ND and NZ layouts** (1,152 additional compared tokens).
- Independent FP32 CPU attention oracles cover FP16/BF16, padded query heads (12→16), branching masks, ragged prefixes, nonconsecutive pages, and a page-crossing draft block. Cache tests cover two layers and overlapping source/destination cycles in ND/NZ.
- A fresh backend import with the older kernel package succeeds without loading the new mask module, checking that the dependency is lazy.
- Ruff/isort, kernel Black checks, `git diff --check`, Mintlify build validation, and broken-link checks passed.

For MLA baseline comparisons, use `ASCEND_USE_FIA=true` on both sides: the legacy paged MLA decoder and FIA round BF16 results differently. Exact greedy text also varies on near-tied free-form continuations across verification shapes. In a diagnostic prompt requesting ten integers, token 33 after the requested list ranked token 1679 over 9081 by 0.0625 log-prob in the baseline; depth=8 reversed the ordering. The second batch agreed again. The registered MLA matrix uses a continuing sequence for this prompt so the full 48-token comparison stays inside the specified task. Prompts and log-prob deltas are recorded in the validation artifacts. CPU-oracle numerical checks independently validate attention semantics.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_ngram_corpus.py \
  test/registered/npu/basic_function/speculative_inference/test_npu_ngram_attention.py

SGLANG_TEST_NGRAM_MODEL=/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B \
python test/registered/npu/basic_function/speculative_inference/test_npu_ngram.py

SGLANG_TEST_NGRAM_MLA_MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 \
python test/registered/npu/basic_function/speculative_inference/test_npu_ngram_mla.py
```

The matrices exercise min breadth 2, max breadth 4, PROB matching, trie depth 8, capacity 64, an external three-document JSONL corpus, SAM budgets 4/11, and the exact external corpus token limit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Observed speedup is limited to identical-request replay on Qwen3-4B, with answer differences. Unseen GSM8K first-pass requests are slower. These results do not establish accuracy-preserving acceleration or a general GSM8K speedup.**

Machine 151, Ascend910_9362, CANN 9.1.0 (A3 B083 image), PyTorch 2.10.0 and torch-npu 2.10.0.post6, TP=1. Tested framework `d07bde5338485bb3f6344683e21dccdd02b5a5cb` with kernel `674b503190c98c4114fa6c26806d36824cb736aa`. The reverted `spec.py` contains no runtime change. Eight relevant deployed framework/kernel source files were checked against these revisions.

![NGRAM throughput: unseen requests versus identical-request replay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/McZyWu/sgl-sglang/c60552cfb0fdb23fade1965103746fa2ed3b4fc7/ngram-npu-performance.png)

The chart includes negative results. Bars are arithmetic mean token throughput; error bars show the observed range across two fresh-engine runs for Qwen3-4B. Qwen3-0.6B has one 64-question run per case; MLA has one 16-question pilot per case. Multipliers compare NGRAM with the native-attention graph baseline.

- **Protocol:** local GSM8K, 5-shot raw completions, seed-42 shuffled test subset, greedy decoding, batch size 1, maximum 1,024 output tokens. This is a performance subset, not a full or official model accuracy evaluation.
- **Fair baseline:** ordinary decoding retains full NPU decode graphs and overlap scheduling. A second ordinary baseline sets `ASCEND_USE_FIA=true` to compare the FIA numerical path. Radix caching is enabled in every case. At these measured revisions, NGRAM used eager execution and synchronous scheduling; no draft model was loaded. These performance results predate MHA graph support.
- **Timing:** synchronized `Engine.generate` wall time, including prefill and detokenization, excluding model loading and four disjoint training warmups. The first measured pass uses unseen test requests. The second repeats exactly the same requests in the same order; the online trie can reuse their previous outputs.
- **NGRAM configuration:** draft-token count 12, capacity 10,000,000, min/max BFS breadth 1/10, BFS matching, trie depth 18, no external corpus for the chart. Qwen3-4B was repeated on physical devices 0 and 2 with reversed case order; comparisons are paired within each device/run.

Qwen3-4B **replay** results, 64 questions in each run:

| Run | Native graph token/s | FIA graph token/s | NGRAM token/s | NGRAM/native | NGRAM/FIA | Same-batch wall-time speedup vs native / FIA |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 90.74 | 96.51 | 131.86 | 1.45x | 1.37x | 1.61x / 1.24x |
| 2 | 100.73 | 94.22 | 141.67 | 1.41x | 1.50x | 1.56x / 1.37x |

Qwen3-4B average generated tokens per verification increased from **2.01** on the first pass to **8.23** on replay; accepted/proposed draft-token ratio increased from **9.01%** to **64.94%**. This reuse dependence is material to the speedup.

Strict final-answer accuracy counts for the same performance requests:

| Model / coverage | Pass | Native graph correct | FIA graph correct | NGRAM correct |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 64 questions | First | 21/64 | 18/64 | 21/64 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 64 questions | Replay | 21/64 | 19/64 | 19/64 |
| Qwen3-4B, 64 questions, both runs | First | 55/64 | 55/64 | 54/64 |
| Qwen3-4B, 64 questions, both runs | Replay | 54/64 | 54/64 | 53/64 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8, 16-question pilot | First | 5/16 | 5/16 | 6/16 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8, 16-question pilot | Replay | 5/16 | 5/16 | 5/16 |

For Qwen3-4B replay, 2/64 NGRAM token sequences differ from the FIA graph baseline in both runs. One baseline-correct response reaches the 1,024-token cap without a strict final answer, accounting for 53/64 versus 54/64. Native attention and FIA also produce different continuations. Numerical/verification-shape differences require further accuracy investigation; the earlier curated token-equivalence regressions do not imply general free-form output equivalence.

The external-corpus trial used only the first 256 GSM8K **training** documents, with SAM budget 4. It did not improve first-pass performance. Replay throughput was 101.72 token/s for Qwen3-0.6B (64 questions), 89.44 for Qwen3-4B (64 questions), and 48.81 for the MLA pilot (16 questions), all below their native graph baselines. The MLA SAM-budget-11 pilot was also slower. No external-corpus speedup is claimed.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Cut LTX-2.3 per-block elementwise work (contiguous AdaLN values, gate-folded masks, vectorized head gate)
issues.body:
Branch: mick/ltx23-block-elementwise (on main 02b983603d), commits 08f4c834c3, 84eaed7e83

## Motivation

LTX-2.3 runs its guidance passes two per CFG rank, so the DiT batch is 2. Three elementwise costs in every block are small at batch 1 and add up at batch 2:

1. `get_ada_values` unbinds a `[B, T, k, D]` sum. With B > 1 every value is strided, so `_ltx2_modulate` copies each scale and shift row to contiguous memory. That is 12 copy launches per block.
2. The modality pass masks the a2v / v2a outputs with a 0/1 per-sample mask, which is a full-size multiply before the gated residual.
3. Gated attention computes `out * (2 * sigmoid(gate_logits))`. The `[B, T, H, 1]` gate is broadcast over the head dim, which PyTorch runs as a non-vectorized strided kernel (26 us at 2x1536x32x128), plus a separate doubling pass. There are six of these per block.

## Modifications

- `get_ada_values` sums value-major (`[k, B, T, D]` via `torch.add(..., out=)`), so every value is contiguous. The audio-video cross-attention tables reuse it instead of an inline copy of the same sum.
- The 0/1 mask commutes with the gate, so it now scales the `[B, T, D]` gate.
- `kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/head_gate_triton.py`: `head_gate_mul` takes the eager `sigmoid(gate_logits)` and applies the doubling and the product in fp32 with one bf16 rounding, which is what eager does. `LTX2Attention` uses it when the attention output is contiguous and keeps the eager expression otherwise.

All three keep the same operations on the same values, so outputs are bitwise identical.

## Tests

- `test_ltx2_ada_values_layout.py`: the value-major values are contiguous and bitwise equal to the old formula (fp32 and bf16 tables, T = 1 and T > 1). A 0/1 mask on the gate equals the mask on the output, bitwise.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_head_gate.py`: `head_gate_mul` is bitwise equal to eager for 4-D and flattened inputs over 4 shapes. Strided, mismatched and fp32 inputs are rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

4xB300 (2 GPUs), LTX-2.3 two-stage 768x512x121, 30 steps, and LTX-2 two-stage: MP4s of 4 requests each are byte-identical (md5) with and without these commits (measured together with the Q/K norm-RoPE vectorization PR).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`head_gate_mul` on B300: 2x1536x32x128 26.2 to 7.8 us, 2x126x32x64 7.4 to 4.5 us, 2x1536x32x64 16.5 to 6.2 us. With the Q/K norm-RoPE PR, LTX-2.3 stage-1 steps go from 97.2 ms to 91.8 ms, and stage 1 from 2.918 s to 2.754 s (synced stage timing).

issues.body: Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Qwen-Image-2.1 — adapt the existing SGLang Diffusion pipeline for Ascend*). ## Motivation Qwen-Image 2.1 already runs on Ascend through `torch_npu`, but two hot paths in the DiT stay on the slow eager implementations: `QwenImage21Attention` forces the native fp32 QK RMSNorm on every platform, and the complex RoPE goes through the complex64 multiply path. This PR routes both to the CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`: - `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`. - `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul(..., rotary_mode="interleave")` for the complex RoPE, with the cos/sin tables prepared once per layout and cached. Cos/sin for `npu_rotary_mul` must be expanded with `repeat_interleave(2)`; a plain `cat((c, c), -1)` pairs the wrong frequencies. The previously attempted Triton fast-path enablement on NPU is **not** part of this change: the QK-norm+RoPE Triton kernel is not bit-exact for sequence lengths ≥ 1024 and is 60–95× slower than the eager chain on Ascend. The three kernel files touched by that attempt are restored to their pre-enablement state. The result is full Qwen-Image 2.1 coverage on one A3 chip: text-to-image, single- and multi-reference editing, transparent RGBA output, and local recolor, with NPU CI cases and baselines. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py` - `QwenImage21Attention`: `force_native=not current_platform.is_npu()` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`, so NPU dispatches to `npu_rms_norm` (bit-identical to the native fp32 path in our measurements). - `apply_rope`: NPU branch using `npu_rotary_mul` with cached cos/sin. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/activation/silu_mul_bitexact.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/complex_rope_triton.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_triton.py` - Revert the previous Triton enablement on NPU: restore the CUDA-only guards, drop the `contextlib.nullcontext()` device branch, and remove the added `contextlib` imports. The files are byte-identical to the state before `7e2e7145fa`. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/testcase_configs_npu.py` - Five `qwen_image21_*` NPU cases with the same sampling contract (1024×1024, png, 40 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, `quality="lossless"`): t2i, single-reference edit, two-reference edit, transparent output, and local recolor. - All five set `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit; the t2i case is switched on together with the NPU GT pin in a follow-up commit once the GT-gen workflow has published its image. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json` - Baselines for the five new cases. - `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/prefetch_input_image.py` - Also cache the second multi-image reference and export `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu.yml` - Run the input prefetch before `gen_diffusion_ci_outputs`, so the reference edit cases can produce their published images. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` - `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-2.1.mdx` - Add Ascend to the hardware picker note and the recommended-hardware table (no separate platform section, matching the Qwen-Image cookbook layout). - `docs/src/snippets/configs/Qwen/qwen-image-2.1.jsx` - Add Ascend A3 to the deployment picker: Torch SDPA only, resident placement, `--warmup-mode request`. ## Verification CI cases - All five `qwen_image21_*` cases run end-to-end with `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit, so the PR CI does not depend on a GT that does not exist yet. issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: HIP flat RoPE kernel with one cos/sin load and int64 offsets, bitwise unchanged
issues.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 run RoPE (forward on q, inverse on the attention output) through `apply_rotary_emb_flat_kernel`, the batched 3D path that DeepseekV4 enables on HIP. The kernel has two problems:
- For every (token, head) row it gathers cos and sin with two strided 64-element loads and builds the rotated term with `tl.where` + `tl.flip`. This costs 7-31% of its time at prefill sizes.
- Its token offsets are int32, so it writes out of bounds once n·H·512 reaches 2³¹ (e.g. 65536 tokens at 128 heads per rank).

## Modifications

All changes are inside `apply_rotary_emb_flat_kernel` (+11/−18):
- Load each row's 64 interleaved cos/sin values once and split the real and imaginary parts in registers.
- Compute with explicit `tl.fma`: round the sine product, then one fma. The compiler already produced this rounding for `x * cos + x_rot`, and `fused_q_norm_rope` uses it on HIP, so the output is bitwise equal.
- Make the token index int64.

The launch (16 rows and 1 warp per program) is unchanged.

An earlier revision of this PR replaced the kernel with a 3D tile kernel and a launch-config function (+47/−55). That revision is not faster overall (mixed at 32 and 64 heads, slower at 128 heads; table below), so this revision keeps the existing kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

| check | result |
|---|---|
| vs the previous kernel, whole tensor: 3 layouts × H {1, 16, 32, 64, 128} × n {1 ... 65536, including the 45-192-row verify/draft sizes} × forward / inverse × positions int64 / int32 / none (1176 cases) | bitwise equal |
| vs the previous kernel: 57 DeepSeek-V4.1 production cases (prefill, SWA tail, verify, draft; production rope tables), and the production entry `fused_rope_inplace` | bitwise equal |
| `test_dsv4_q_rope_store.py`, `test_hip_flash_mla_aiter_sparse.py`, `test_v41_kv_store.py` | 19 passed, 47 subtests passed, the same as without this PR. 17 `test_v41_kv_store.py` subtests fail with and without it: the fused K-norm-RoPE store JIT kernel does not build under ROCm 7.2.4 (32-bit `__shfl_xor_sync` mask) |

For 65536 x 128, where the previous kernel overflows, the reference is the previous kernel run in chunks below 2³¹. Every output is also checked against an fp32 reference.
